newsitem.title: USA: Carolina Power says 268,000 still lack power.
newsitem.headline: Carolina Power says 268,000 still lack power.

text.p: Carolina Power & Light Co said Monday the lights were back on at 462,000 of its customers who lost power during Hurricane Fran, but that 268,000 were still having to cope without.
"It's probably still a week or more until we get power back to everyone. We serve some very rural areas," said company spokesman Mike Hughes.
"We've got every available crew east of the Mississippi and some from west of the Mississippi working on this, some coming from as far away as Illinois and New Jersey," he said.
There are currently 5,000 linemen and tree cutters helping restore power. "And we expect to add another 1,500 workers today," he said.
Hughes said five of Carolina Power's high-voltage transmission lines were still down.
The company said Friday the storm, which hit the North Carolina coast late Thursday and roared right through the heart of its service territory, knocked out about 40 transmission lines.
"And we estimate that we'll have to replace about 1,000 miles of distribution lines and 4,000 poles," he said.
Brunswick 1, one of two nuclear reactors Carolina Power shut Thursday as a precaution ahead of Fran, is to restart today, putting power back on the grid by Tuesday, Hughes said.

The adjacent Brunswick 2 unit will begin restart later this week. The two units, which produce a combined 1,521 megawatts (MW) of power, are at Southport, N.C., near Cape Fear, where Fran made landfall.
Despite the downed generating facilities, the fact that so many customers are still off the grid is dampening demand.

"We don't see any problem meeting demand," said Hughes, adding peak demand Monday was estimated at 7,500 to 7,600 MW, "condsiderably lower than usual for a day like today, when the temperature is expected to hit 89 (degrees Fahrenheit)."
Hughes said the utility did not expect to have an overall damage estimate from the storm until all cleanup and restoration work are completed.
Fran knocked out power to about two-thirds of the Carolina Power's 1.1 million customers, most of them in southeastern North Carolina.
-- J Jelter, New York Power Desk, +1 212 859 1621
